record.paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
record.original_question: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2 and M = S × R. If l_- and l_+ are weighted multicurves on S that fill S, is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M whose convex-core boundary has measured bending laminations l_- and l_+?

evidence.quote: Question 9.1. If l− and l+ are weighted multi-curves which fill S, is there a unique GHMC AdS structure h on M such that l− and l+ are the measured bending laminations of the boundary of the convex core?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface of genus at least $2$, and let $M = S \times \mathbb{R}$. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter (AdS) structure on $M$ is a Lorentzian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ such that $M$ contains a closed spacelike Cauchy surface (a closed embedded spacelike surface meeting every inextendible timelike curve exactly once) and is maximal among such manifolds with respect to isometric embedding. Each GHMC AdS manifold contains a unique minimal nonempty closed convex subset $C(M)$, called the convex core; when $M$ is not Fuchsian, the boundary $\partial C(M)$ has two connected components, each a pleated spacelike surface homeomorphic to $S$, whose pleating data are recorded by two measured geodesic laminations $\mu_-$ and $\mu_+$ on $S$ called the measured bending laminations of the lower and upper boundary components of the convex core.

A weighted multicurve on $S$ is a measured geodesic lamination whose support is a disjoint union of finitely many simple closed geodesics, each carrying a positive real weight; equivalently, it is a rational measured lamination. Two measured laminations $\ell_-, \ell_+$ on $S$ are said to fill $S$ if for every nontrivial simple closed curve $\gamma$ on $S$, the sum of intersection numbers $i(\gamma, \ell_-) + i(\gamma, \ell_+)$ is strictly positive.

Question: Given any pair of weighted multicurves $\ell_-$ and $\ell_+$ on $S$ that fill $S$, is there a unique GHMC anti-de Sitter structure $h$ on $M$ whose lower and upper convex-core measured bending laminations are exactly $\ell_-$ and $\ell_+$, respectively?
artifact.category_tag: Anti-de Sitter geometry / convex core bending laminations
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of a GHMC AdS structure realizing any pair of filling measured laminations as convex-core bending laminations was established by Bonsante–Schlenker, who also proved uniqueness near the Fuchsian locus. Subsequent work has extended uniqueness to small enough filling pairs and to rational laminations in particular regimes, and recent papers (e.g., on rigidity near the Fuchsian locus and on quasi-Fuchsian analogues by Dular–Schlenker) have established related uniqueness statements. However, unconditional uniqueness for arbitrary filling weighted multicurves in the AdS setting does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature found, so the problem appears to be partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Rigidity of anti-de Sitter (2+1)-spacetimes with convex boundary near the Fuchsian locus
status_evidence.snippet: The realization of pleating laminations was shown by Bonsante–Schlenker, where the rigidity near the Fuchsian locus was also deduced. Except that, the rigidity parts of these problems remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is known and uniqueness is known only near the Fuchsian locus; general rigidity remains open.

status_evidence.title: Convex co-compact hyperbolic manifolds are determined by their pleating lamination
status_evidence.snippet: For small enough measured laminations that fill the surface, there exists a unique GHMC AdS manifold with specified measured bending laminations on the upper and lower boundary components of the convex core.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness has been established only for sufficiently small filling laminations in the AdS case.

status_evidence.title: Polyhedral surfaces in anti-de Sitter (2+1)-spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Rational laminations can be uniquely realized... small enough pairs of filling measured laminations can be realized uniquely as the measured pleating lamination of the boundary of the convex core near the Fuchsian locus.
status_evidence.claim: Partial uniqueness results exist for rational laminations and near the Fuchsian locus.
